subtitle: Recognize mental health stigma when it appears, respond with respect and protect each person’s choice, privacy and fair work expectations.
scope: For DHS staff learning about mental health, communication and ordinary workplace or service interactions. Original practice cases support reflection, not diagnosis, treatment, crisis-response certification or a legal determination. Actual service, employment, privacy, reporting and emergency responsibilities remain. Use private reflection or practice; no personal health disclosure or live work submission is required. This optional learning does not count toward DHS-required training credits unless management, a director or DHS leadership expressly approves an exception.
introTranscript: Mental health is part of health. A person’s mental health condition does not tell us their whole story, ability, judgment or preferred support. This course examines how labels can enter everyday explanations and choices, even when the original purpose is to be helpful. You will follow original practice staff and service examples, replace unsupported assumptions with relevant questions, compare meanings of support and keep appropriate responsibilities clear. Respectful conversation can matter in itself. Clinical care and formal employment decisions belong with their qualified or authorized roles. Learn at your own pace without disclosing personal health information.

lessons.title: See the person beyond a label
lessons.summary: Separate mental health, a stated condition, observed circumstances and an unsupported judgment about a person.
lessons.objective: Distinguish a stated health condition from an inferred diagnosis or ability judgment.
objectives: Distinguish a stated health condition from an inferred diagnosis or ability judgment.
Explain how an unsupported label can affect an ordinary staff choice.
Choose a response that addresses the present situation without requiring personal disclosure.
takeaways: Mental health includes more than the presence or absence of a diagnosed condition.
A single behavior does not establish a diagnosis, cause or ability profile.
Ask about a relevant task or offer of support without demanding a private history.
lessons.statement: A health label cannot supply the missing facts about a person or a task.

image.caption: A colleague stands beside a whiteboard while another gestures toward the discussion. The photograph does not establish anyone’s health status.

intro.heading: Begin with what is actually known
intro.body:
Mental health includes emotional, psychological and social well-being. The National Institute of Mental Health explains that it is more than the absence of mental illness. A person can have concerns, strengths, relationships and ordinary responsibilities together. Staff learning does not require placing someone in a healthy-or-unhealthy category. Nor does it require a colleague to disclose a diagnosis before being treated with respect.

In a DHS team, Avery asks to move a planning conversation from a noisy shared area to a quieter room. Another colleague says, “Avery seems unstable today,” and suggests removing Avery from the task. The known information is much narrower: a request for another conversation setting. No health condition, cause, job inability or safety risk has been established. The label fills those gaps with a personal judgment. It could alter an opportunity before anyone has examined what the task requires.

Stigma, as used in this course, involves discrediting a person through negative meanings attached to a condition or perceived condition. A stereotype is an assumed group characteristic applied without the individual evidence needed for the choice. A discriminatory action or policy violation requires its actual legal or agency process; the course does not adjudicate it. These distinctions let us examine a questionable choice without asserting that we know every motive or have proved a violation.

A relevant response can ask whether the quieter room is available and how the conversation can proceed. It does not need to ask what is wrong with Avery or announce a medical explanation. If a disability- or medical-condition-related employment request is made, the actual accommodation process also matters. That process is distinct from everyday courtesy, and later lessons explain its responsibilities.

For personal understanding, consider a time when an unfamiliar request received an easy explanation in your mind. What did you observe, and what did you supply? You can examine that distinction privately. No one must share a health experience, defend their reaction publicly or receive a personal-development score to learn from it.

inThisLesson: Mental health as part of health.
lessons.keyStatement: Describe the relevant circumstance before interpreting the person.

flashcards.back: A broad part of health and well-being, not a yes-or-no staff classification.
What was said or occurred in the situation, kept separate from an invented cause.
An assumed group trait used in place of the individual evidence a choice needs.
Personal understanding that can remain unrecorded and need not disclose a health history.

items.title: A quieter room is a specific request
items.body: Ask whether the room or another appropriate arrangement works for this conversation. The request does not itself establish why Avery needs it or whether an employment accommodation process has begun. Attention to the actual task can improve the encounter without turning staff into diagnosticians.

items.title: A diagnosis would still be incomplete information
items.body: Even if Avery voluntarily stated a condition, that would not prove inability to handle the planning task. Conditions and individual circumstances vary. Use relevant work evidence and actual responsible processes instead of translating the condition into a list of presumed weaknesses.

items.title: Respect does not depend on proving a good intention
items.body: A colleague may have intended to be protective. The proposed removal still needs examination. Discuss the unsupported assumption and the effect of the choice without demanding a confession about motives or declaring every person who used the phrase a particular kind of person.

tabs.label: A behavior-based label
tabs.body: Calling Avery unstable converts a setting request into a conclusion about the person. Removing the assignment then makes that conclusion consequential. Return to what was actually requested and the work requirements; a dramatic description cannot supply medical, ability or safety evidence.

tabs.label: A condition-based prediction
tabs.body: If a diagnosis is later volunteered, predicting unreliable work from it repeats the same reasoning problem with a different starting fact. The condition is real information about health, but it is not a finding about this assignment. Fair treatment keeps relevant performance evidence and appropriate supports in view.

tabs.label: A task-focused response
tabs.body: Avery’s request can be considered in relation to the conversation setting, available arrangements and actual responsibilities. This leaves room for a relevant employment request or another concern without forcing a health explanation. The first conversation becomes more useful because it addresses the situation that was presented.

check.question: What does Avery’s request establish in this example?
check.correct: Avery has asked for a different conversation setting; staff should address the relevant task without inventing a diagnosis or inability.
wrong: Avery has a mental health condition and should leave the assignment.
The colleague’s helpful intention proves that removal is fair.
Avery must disclose health information before any courtesy is considered.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response keeps observed information distinct from conclusions that need evidence or an actual responsible process.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A room request does not establish a diagnosis or job inability. Helpful intent cannot justify an unsupported removal. A private health account is not a prerequisite to ordinary courtesy. Examine the presented request and retain actual processes if another responsibility arises.

items.text: Avery asked for a quieter conversation setting.
The shared area is where the conversation was planned.
Avery cannot manage the project.
A mental health diagnosis explains the request.
Which available setting works for this task?
Has an actual medical-condition-related employment request been made?

lessons.next: Examine how the wording of an explanation can change the response.

scenario.context: Practice DHS planning: a colleague proposes moving Avery off the assignment because the room request seems unusual. No ability or safety finding exists.
options: Address the setting request and task requirements without a personal diagnosis; use actual processes if a separate responsibility arises.
Remove Avery now because caution makes the inference accurate.
Ask Avery to disclose a diagnosis in the team conversation.
responses: This retains the task and individual dignity without claiming unknown facts.
Caution cannot supply the missing individual evidence or authority.
Public disclosure is unnecessary for the presented setting question.

lessons.transfer: Privately separate an observed request from an explanation you might be tempted to supply. A practice example is sufficient.

move.control: Keep the observed circumstance and the proposed consequence distinct.
move.failure: A label becomes the reason for a consequential choice without examining relevant evidence.
move.next: Practice a task-focused response in the practice room conversation; no live disclosure is required.

lessons.title: Use language that informs rather than defines
lessons.summary: Choose accurate, respectful wording without turning a condition into an insult or imposing a single identity style.
lessons.objective: Identify wording that substitutes a health label for a specific description.
objectives: Identify wording that substitutes a health label for a specific description.
Choose a respectful revision that preserves the relevant meaning.
Explain why a personal story or language preference cannot be required as proof of inclusion.
takeaways: Describe the circumstance rather than use a diagnosis as an insult or shorthand.
A person’s stated preference matters without becoming the rule for everyone.
Inviting a story does not create an obligation to disclose it.
lessons.statement: Respectful language can be clear about the issue without making the person the problem.

image.caption: The whiteboard contains diagrams and notes. Its visible marks do not provide evidence about the participants’ diagnoses or emotions.

intro.heading: Keep the useful meaning and remove the unsupported label
intro.body:
In the practice team’s planning note, a colleague writes that the changing draft is “bipolar” and that a careful colleague is “OCD.” The note does not describe a clinical condition. It borrows health terms to explain inconsistency and attention to detail. That can blur the actual issue and attach a negative or trivial meaning to people who have those conditions. A more informative note says what changed in the draft and which review task needs clarification.

CDC communication guidance supports neutral, respectful wording and attention to the audience. Its mental-health section distinguishes diagnosed conditions from distress and offers person-focused wording. The related NIOSH guidance also recognizes that people do not always agree on a preferred identity style. A chosen description can be respected without making every person use the same words. Do not infer a diagnosis from distress or demand that a person explain a language preference through medical details.

A revision could read, “The draft uses two different response deadlines; the team needs to confirm which one applies.” This preserves the issue and makes a useful next step possible. Calling the draft bipolar does neither. Similarly, “The colleague checked the citations against the sources” describes the work. It does not trivialize obsessive-compulsive disorder or imply that the colleague has it. This lesson is about meaningful wording, not banning the names of actual conditions in appropriate contexts.

A staff event organizer proposes that everyone tell a personal mental-health story to show the team is welcoming. NIOSH guidance cautions against pressuring people to share. A participant may value privacy, have no story they wish to tell or prefer another way to participate. The team can discuss language and fair practices using practice examples. Voluntary sharing, when chosen, still needs an appropriate setting and understanding of how information will be used; a group invitation is not permission for redistribution.

Privately notice a phrase you use casually. What does it help the listener understand? Can a precise description carry the meaning more clearly? This personal inquiry has value without a public pledge, a confession or a recorded account of health.

inThisLesson: Accurate descriptions of drafts and work.
Story invitations with a genuine choice.
lessons.keyStatement: A precise description can preserve the concern while removing an unnecessary health judgment.

flashcards.back: A clear account of the draft, action or question that needs attention.
A health description used accurately and relevantly, rather than as an insult or invented diagnosis.
A person’s chosen language, not evidence that everyone shares it.
A personal account shared by choice, without pressure or automatic permission for wider use.

items.title: Keep the issue visible
items.body: Removing bipolar from the planning note should not erase the contradictory deadlines. State both versions and the need for an authorized clarification. Respectful wording works best when it helps the reader understand the actual problem rather than leaves a vague positive sentence.

items.title: Do not turn a preference into a test
items.body: Someone may prefer a person-focused term, another a different accurate description. Ask when relevant and respect the choice. A colleague need not provide diagnostic proof or defend their identity wording before the conversation can proceed.

items.title: An invitation needs a reasonable alternative
items.body: A practice exercise, ordinary discussion or private reflection can support the learning purpose without personal health stories. Calling disclosure optional while judging silent participants as uncommitted removes the choice. Keep engagement separate from the amount of private information provided.

tabs.label: A softened insult
tabs.body: Changing the note to “a little bipolar” keeps the clinical term as a metaphor and still leaves the two deadlines unexplained. A gentler tone cannot fix the missing meaning. Describe the conflicting instructions and the actual clarification needed.

tabs.label: A vague positive label
tabs.body: Calling the colleague “special” removes the original term but adds little about the work. It can also sound patronizing. A specific account of the citation check recognizes what was done and lets colleagues understand the contribution without a health or personality judgment.

tabs.label: A precise task account
tabs.body: The revised note identifies contradictory response dates and the citation review. That is clearer for the next reader and avoids unrelated health meanings. Accuracy and dignity support each other; the team can still discuss actual conditions when relevant and appropriately shared.

check.question: Which revision best addresses the practice planning note?
check.correct: Describe the contradictory deadlines and citation review accurately, without diagnostic shorthand or a compulsory personal story.
wrong: Keep the diagnostic term if it is meant affectionately.
Remove every condition name, including relevant accurate discussions of health.
Require everyone to disclose a condition to agree on preferred language.
check.feedbackCorrect: The revision preserves what matters to the work and respects individual information choices.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Affectionate intent does not make diagnostic shorthand informative. A blanket ban would prevent appropriate accurate discussion of conditions. Compulsory disclosure makes private health information a participation gate. Use precise wording and genuine individual choice.

items.text: The draft lists two response dates that need clarification.
The colleague verified citations against the sources.
The draft is bipolar.
Checking a citation proves the colleague has OCD.
A participant chooses practice instead of a personal story.
A person’s stated language preference is respected without requiring medical proof.

lessons.next: Consider why the same offer of support can carry different meanings.

scenario.context: Practice team event: the organizer calls personal stories optional, then asks managers to list everyone who declined.
scenario.prompt: Which change preserves the learning purpose?
options: Keep the list because participation proves a healthy culture.
Provide practice or private ways to learn and avoid judging commitment from a choice not to disclose.
Cancel all mental-health learning because disclosure can be private.
responses: A list turns a private choice into a participation judgment.
This retains learning while making the information choice real.
The subject can be taught meaningfully without compulsory personal stories.

lessons.transfer: Revise a practice label into a specific description. Notice privately whether the revision changes your own understanding.

move.control: Keep relevant meaning, individual preference and information choice together.
move.failure: A kinder-sounding label or an optional story becomes another unsupported judgment.
move.next: Use the practice planning note to practice a precise revision without disclosing a health experience.

lessons.title: Offer support with a real choice
lessons.summary: Understand different meanings of care, listen without demanding a private account and keep clinical advice with qualified care.
lessons.objective: Compare two meanings the people describe of support without assigning them to a whole group.
objectives: Compare two meanings the people describe of support without assigning them to a whole group.
Choose a fitting offer that allows acceptance, discussion or refusal.
Distinguish ordinary support from diagnosis, treatment advice or a guaranteed confidentiality promise.
takeaways: An offer of support can carry meanings shaped by personal experience.
Listening and a fitting choice can matter without gathering a health history.
Clinical care, immediate emergencies and actual formal duties remain distinct from an ordinary offer.
lessons.statement: Care becomes more fitting when the other person can help define what is useful.

image.caption: Two colleagues take part in a whiteboard discussion. Their gestures do not establish how either person prefers to receive support.

intro.heading: Widen the meaning of a helpful response
intro.body:
In this conversation, Kai tells Mira that a recent period has been difficult and asks to speak privately. Mira immediately offers three solutions and says they should put the matter behind them. Kai becomes quiet. That silence does not prove that Mira helped, that Kai rejected care or that either person has a particular mental health condition. The response has not yet been understood from Kai’s perspective.

In this example, Mira voluntarily explains that she grew up learning to show care through quick practical action. Kai voluntarily explains learning that a thoughtful listener makes room for the person’s own account before offering a solution. These supplied histories create different meanings of care: prompt action for Mira, space to understand for Kai. They do not identify national, disability or other group patterns. Neither person must provide this history in a real encounter. The case makes the contrast visible so you can examine a first interpretation.

Mira can keep her wish to help while widening how she expresses it. She might ask whether Kai wants a listener, help with a specific work matter or information about a support resource. Kai can decline or choose another arrangement. The conversation does not become a therapy session simply because it is private. Mira should not diagnose Kai, suggest changing medication or promise that nothing can ever be shared under any circumstances. Actual duties and information handling still apply.

The Council of Europe describes learned meanings as varied and contextual, not fixed traits of everyone in a group. This provides a useful educational lens for comparing the two histories. The wider understanding matters for its own sake: Mira can recognize why listening has value even if no immediate task changes. It does not place her on an intercultural assessment continuum or require Kai’s gratitude.

NIMH describes individual self-care and qualified professional help as different parts of supporting mental health. An ordinary colleague need not prescribe either. Information can be offered without making use of it a test of commitment. If there is immediate physical danger, use emergency assistance; NIMH identifies 911 for life-threatening situations and 988 for emotional or mental-health crisis support. The practice discussion here is not an emergency simulation and cannot replace actual emergency procedures.

For private reflection, consider what support has meant in your experience. Could listening, privacy, action or a chosen resource carry another reasonable meaning? You can learn from the contrast without recording an intimate account or testing it on a colleague.

inThisLesson: Care as action and as room to understand.
Private understanding beyond immediate task results.
lessons.keyStatement: Another meaning can widen the offer without erasing your wish to help.

flashcards.back: A voluntarily stated interpretation within the example, not a group profile.
Support connected to what the person wants to discuss, with a real choice.
Assessment and treatment by qualified care professionals, not a colleague’s informal diagnosis.
An ordinary conversation cannot promise that actual duties never apply.

items.title: Ask before giving solutions
items.body: Kai may want practical help, a listening conversation or neither at the present moment. An initial question lets Mira discover the purpose rather than impose her usual method. It is not a demand for Kai to explain a diagnosis or the entire history of the difficulty.

items.title: A quiet response remains uncertain
items.body: Mira has received little information about the effect of her quick solutions. She can ask whether the conversation has been useful without requiring praise. If Kai does not wish to continue, that choice is not a finding that the help succeeded or that Kai lacks commitment.

items.title: A colleague is not the treating professional
items.body: Mira can offer resource information and appropriate work support. Choosing a treatment, interpreting symptoms or changing medication goes beyond this learning role. A private conversation also does not cancel actual reporting, emergency or accommodation responsibilities when they apply.

tabs.label: Action before understanding
tabs.body: Mira’s list of solutions expresses the care she learned, but it can close Kai’s intended conversation before the purpose is known. Asking about the desired support creates a wider response. It keeps practical help available while recognizing that room to be heard can itself be meaningful.

tabs.label: Listening as compulsory disclosure
tabs.body: Demanding a complete personal account before offering help changes listening into a condition of support. Kai’s privacy and choice remain. A focused question about what would be useful can be enough for the ordinary offer; any actual formal information request belongs with its responsible process.

tabs.label: Choice within a wider frame
tabs.body: Mira understands why Kai may value time to speak, and asks which kind of support is wanted. She can listen appropriately, discuss a relevant work matter or provide resource information without deciding on treatment. The adapted behavior follows a changed understanding of care, not a prediction based on identity.

check.question: Which response best follows the wider understanding of care?
check.correct: Ask what kind of support would be useful, allow a genuine choice and keep treatment and actual duties with their appropriate roles.
wrong: Give advice until Kai agrees, because action always demonstrates care.
Ask for a full mental-health history to prove that listening is needed.
Promise that nothing can ever be shared, regardless of actual duties or danger.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response widens the meaning of care while retaining choice and responsible boundaries.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Persistent advice makes Mira’s preferred method the test of care. A full health history is unnecessary for an ordinary listening offer. An absolute secrecy promise could conflict with actual obligations or emergency needs. Offer relevant support without taking over a clinical or formal role.

sorting.heading: Locate the response and its purpose

items.text: Ask whether Kai wants a listener or information about a resource.
Allow Kai to decline the offer without judging commitment.
Interpret silence as proof of recovery.
Tell Kai how to change medication based on the conversation.
Use emergency assistance for immediate physical danger.
Carry an actual medical-condition-related employment request through its proper process.

lessons.next: Connect respectful support with fair expectations and actual employment processes.

scenario.context: Practice conversation: Mira learns that quick advice and room to speak have different meanings for her and Kai. Kai has not asked for treatment advice.
scenario.prompt: Which response follows the new understanding?
options: Insist on quick solutions so Kai learns the right way to receive care.
Ask for diagnostic proof before listening.
Offer a listening conversation or relevant practical help by choice, without diagnosis or a secrecy guarantee.
responses: This keeps one meaning as the universal rule and misses the supplied contrast.
Proof is not needed for the ordinary offer and would impose a private-information gate.
This uses the wider meaning to change the response while keeping appropriate boundaries.

lessons.transfer: Privately describe how two meanings of support could change an offer in the Kai–Mira conversation. No personal story is required.

move.control: Keep understanding, choice and the actual role together.
move.failure: An ordinary offer becomes compulsory disclosure, clinical advice or a proof of recovery.
move.next: Practice a fitting offer with the practice case and leave personal reflection unrecorded if you prefer.

lessons.title: Keep fair work expectations and proper accommodation roles
lessons.summary: Examine actual task evidence without stereotypes and recognize a medical-condition-related request through the correct employment process.
lessons.objective: Distinguish specific work evidence from a condition-based prediction of inability or risk.
objectives: Distinguish specific work evidence from a condition-based prediction of inability or risk.
Choose the proper initial response to a medical-condition-related employment request.
Explain why support resources, medical documentation and performance decisions have different roles.
takeaways: A condition does not establish inability or risk without the relevant individual evidence.
An initial accommodation request can use ordinary words; the recipient promptly forwards it and identifies the decision-maker.
Appropriate documentation belongs to the ADA Coordinator, not an informal supervisor health inquiry.
lessons.statement: Fair expectations and appropriate support can be considered together without an identity-based prediction.

image.caption: Colleagues discuss visible diagrams and notes. The photograph provides no basis for assessing anyone’s ability to perform a job.

intro.heading: Examine the task and preserve the actual request process
intro.body:
In an original practice DHS assignment, Rowan has completed the required source checks but one response memo arrived after the agreed handoff. A supervisor learns from Rowan that they have an anxiety-related medical condition and need a change in how competing instructions are provided. The supervisor proposes removing all complex assignments and asking for therapy records before considering the request. Neither proposal follows automatically from the stated condition.

The EEOC’s mental-health technical assistance distinguishes stereotypes from objective individual evidence about job duties or risk. A condition alone does not establish inability to do a task. At the same time, respectful support does not erase actual performance responsibilities. The team can clarify the memo handoff, instructions and appropriate expectations through the actual authorized process. It should not explain the late memo through a diagnosis without evidence or assume that every future assignment will fail.

Rowan has connected a needed work change to a medical condition. Under MMB Policy 1433, an initial request does not require special legal words or a particular initial format. The recipient promptly forwards it to the appropriate decision-maker and, at the same time, tells Rowan who that person is. Actual agency authority matters: the ADA Coordinator decides requests outside supervisors’ or managers’ authority, and consultation applies when issues arise and before a denial. The course invents no DHS delegation or promise of the requested arrangement.

Supervisors and managers must not request medical information or documentation for this accommodation process. Appropriate requests belong to the agency ADA Coordinator. Medical records are not appropriate accommodation documentation and agencies must not request or accept them. This does not erase all documentation: the actual process may appropriately seek relevant information through its designated role. Health information remains confidential under the actual requirements.

MMB’s referral guidance also distinguishes an offer of Employee Assistance Program support from performance evaluation or discipline. The program is voluntary, and using it cannot become the measure of Rowan’s work. A resource offer does not substitute for the accommodation process or establish that a supervisor has approved an arrangement.

For practice, keep three questions separate: what is the documented task issue, what change has been requested, and who has the actual responsibility to act? You can work through the practice case without sharing a diagnosis, employee file or live performance matter.

inThisLesson: Specific task evidence and unsupported predictions.
Support offers distinct from work evaluation.
lessons.keyStatement: Use the relevant task evidence and the actual process rather than a health stereotype.

flashcards.back: A located account of an assignment, requirement or result, not an inferred medical cause.
A communication asking for a work change because of a medical condition; special legal wording is unnecessary.
The actual agency role responsible for the request within delegated authority.
Appropriate accommodation information requests belong to the ADA Coordinator; supervisors do not collect it.

items.title: One late memo is a task matter
items.body: Clarify what was due, what was delivered and what instructions existed. A late memo does not demonstrate that every complex assignment is unsuitable. The actual work process can address expectations while the separate support request receives prompt appropriate handling.

items.title: A request is not an automatic approval
items.body: Recognizing Rowan’s ordinary words begins the actual process; it does not establish that one proposed method is required or effective. Prompt forwarding and decision-maker notice let Rowan know where the request is going. Retain consultation and actual delegated roles instead of an informal supervisor promise.

items.title: Do not gather therapy records
items.body: A supervisor’s wish to understand the request does not create a right to collect private treatment records. Policy 1433 assigns appropriate documentation requests to the ADA Coordinator and excludes medical records from this accommodation process. Relevant work instructions can still be discussed without a clinical history.

tabs.heading: Compare three responses to the assignment

tabs.label: Protective removal
tabs.body: Removing Rowan from every complex task may appear caring, but it assumes inability from the condition rather than examines this work and available support. It also changes opportunity before an actual decision. Preserve relevant expectations and carry the request through the authorized process instead of making health the assignment rule.

tabs.label: Ignoring the request
tabs.body: Treating the late memo solely as a performance issue overlooks Rowan’s separate medical-condition-related request. Actual expectations still matter, but they do not cancel prompt request handling. Clarify the task issue and forward the request with notice; one conversation can recognize both responsibilities without combining their files or purposes.

tabs.label: Separate responsibilities together
tabs.body: The supervisor locates the handoff issue, forwards the request through actual agency authority and identifies the decision-maker to Rowan. Private documentation stays with the appropriate role, and a voluntary support offer stays distinct. This avoids both an automatic exemption from duties and an unsupported prediction of future inability.

check.question: Which initial response best fits Rowan’s request?
check.correct: Clarify relevant task expectations and promptly forward the medical-condition-related request to the appropriate decision-maker, notifying Rowan at the same time and retaining actual agency roles.
wrong: Demand therapy records before forwarding because the supervisor needs to know the diagnosis.
Remove every complex duty immediately because anxiety proves future inability.
Offer counseling instead of carrying the accommodation request forward.
check.feedbackCorrect: This recognizes both the located work matter and the actual accommodation responsibility without inventing a decision.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A supervisor cannot collect the proposed medical records under Policy 1433; appropriate information requests belong to the ADA Coordinator. Removing all complex work predicts inability from a condition. Counseling can be offered separately and voluntarily but cannot replace the accommodation process.

sorting.heading: Separate work, request and unsupported shortcut

items.text: Clarify the memo requirement and handoff instructions.
Use located task evidence rather than an invented medical cause.
Promptly forward the request and simultaneously identify the decision-maker to Rowan.
Keep appropriate accommodation documentation requests with the ADA Coordinator.
Treat use of counseling as the performance measure.
Assume every future assignment will fail because a condition was stated.

lessons.next: Examine how the same labels can affect a service interaction and a protected-class concern.

scenario.context: Practice DHS supervision: Rowan asks for different competing instructions because of an anxiety-related medical condition. The supervisor proposes counseling as the only response.
options: Offer resources only if appropriate and voluntary, while promptly forwarding the request with decision-maker notice through actual authority and clarifying the task issue.
Require counseling attendance before any request is forwarded.
Approve the proposed work change immediately and require therapy records personally.
responses: This preserves the actual request, work expectations and separate support offer.
Counseling is voluntary and cannot become the forwarding gate.
The course establishes neither approval authority nor the requested arrangement, and supervisors do not request accommodation medical documentation.

lessons.transfer: Use the Rowan case to identify the task evidence, requested change and actual responsible process. Do not include live health records.

move.control: Keep expectations, support and formal roles distinct but responsive.
move.failure: A health label replaces task evidence, or a resource offer replaces an actual request process.
move.next: Practice the prompt forwarding and notice response using the practice request; approval and documentation remain with their actual roles.

lessons.title: Keep the service question visible and respond to concerns
lessons.summary: Avoid dismissing a person’s question through a health label and retain appropriate current service and reporting responsibilities.
lessons.objective: Explain how a condition-based credibility judgment can distract from a specific service question.
objectives: Explain how a condition-based credibility judgment can distract from a specific service question.
Choose a response that addresses the person and actual service task without inventing a clinical assessment.
Identify the immediate manager reporting responsibility for an actual protected-class allegation or incident.
takeaways: A mental-health label does not settle the substance of a question or complaint.
A relevant service response and an actual concern process can proceed without becoming a public health discussion.
Managers and supervisors immediately report protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures.
lessons.statement: A concern deserves its actual responsible response rather than an explanation based on a person’s presumed condition.

image.caption: A colleague holds a folder near a whiteboard while another responds. The photograph does not identify a service recipient or a clinical encounter.

intro.heading: Answer the issue without making an unsupported credibility judgment
intro.body:
In an original practice DHS information visit, Jules asks why two notices give different instructions for providing a document. Jules has previously chosen to mention a mental health condition in another conversation. A staff member dismisses the new question as “just the condition talking.” That response does not establish which instruction applies. The conflict between the notices is a real question in the example, regardless of the volunteered condition.

A useful response identifies the two instructions, asks only what is relevant to understand the request and carries the clarification to the responsible service role. It should not demand a treatment update before the information question can be answered. Nor should it distribute the prior health disclosure to everyone handling the draft. Actual service, information and confidentiality requirements continue to apply; a volunteered detail does not create unlimited permission to share it.

This does not mean staff must ignore actual behavior, emergencies or assigned responsibilities. A relevant observed incident follows the actual applicable procedure, and qualified care or emergency assistance may be appropriate in its own context. The practice notice question provides no clinical or safety evidence. Staff should not invent a danger because a condition was named or let the ordinary information task become an informal assessment.

Jules tells a supervisor that a staff member mocked the disclosed condition and refused to consider the notice question for that reason. Under MMB Policy 1436, actual or perceived protected-class concerns are not merely a question of general team courtesy. Managers and supervisors must immediately report all allegations or incidents of protected-class harassment or discrimination to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and comply with agency procedures. Staff and third parties are strongly encouraged to report concerns through the policy’s channels. The course does not make a finding that a violation occurred.

A supervisor’s reporting duty cannot wait for an apology, independent proof, a completed learning activity or a successful consultant conversation. Assigned investigation and corrective responsibilities remain under the actual agency procedures and authority. Ordinary service clarification can continue appropriately without requiring Jules to tell a public health story or making another employee conduct an improvised investigation.

For reflection, examine the distinction between a person’s identity information and the actual content of their question. What did the label replace? A practice analysis can help you understand that pattern without publishing a real complaint, personal history or investigation account.

inThisLesson: The substance of the service question.
Service response and formal process together.
lessons.keyStatement: Keep the question, the relevant evidence and the actual responsibility in view.

flashcards.back: The specific instruction, decision or need that the person has presented.
An unsupported personal label used to dismiss the substance of the question.
Immediate protected-class allegation or incident reporting to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer under Policy 1436.
Actual agency complaint, investigation and corrective procedures within the person’s authority.

accordion.heading: Preserve the response the situation needs

items.title: The notice conflict remains
items.body: The prior health disclosure does not explain why the two notices disagree. Locate the relevant versions and responsible clarification role. Treating the person’s condition as the answer leaves the information problem unresolved and can obscure a needed service response.

items.title: Carry the concern through its actual route
items.body: Jules’s allegation is enough to engage the supervisor’s reporting responsibility; a course or apology cannot replace it. HR, the agency Affirmative Action Officer and other assigned roles act under agency procedures. The learning example makes no independent legal or disciplinary finding.

items.title: Keep service help available appropriately
items.body: A complaint does not make every service question an investigation task. Address the current notice clarification through the appropriate role while the concern follows its own process. Avoid retaliation, unnecessary exposure of personal information or a requirement to withdraw the concern to receive help.

tabs.heading: Compare three accounts of the visit

tabs.label: An identity-based explanation
tabs.body: “The condition explains the complaint” appears to settle uncertainty quickly but does not examine the two notices or the alleged conduct. It replaces both tasks with a prediction about Jules. Relevant service facts and the actual reporting duty remain, even if the health detail was voluntarily shared earlier.

tabs.label: An informal resolution gate
tabs.body: Waiting for the staff member to apologize can delay a supervisor’s immediate Policy 1436 report. An appropriate apology may have its place, but it does not establish that the concern is resolved or change the reporting duty. Do not make Jules negotiate informally before the actual process can proceed.

tabs.label: A responsible parallel response
tabs.body: The supervisor immediately reports the allegation to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follows procedures. The notice issue receives appropriate service clarification, and personal information stays within its proper limits. This can be responsive without a premature finding, a public personal account or an unauthorized investigation.

check.question: Which response best fits the practice visit and allegation?
check.correct: Address the notice question through its responsible service role and have the supervisor immediately report the protected-class allegation to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer under agency procedures.
wrong: Wait for proof that the person’s condition did not cause the question.
Require an apology conversation before the supervisor reports.
Publish the prior health disclosure so every team can judge credibility.
check.feedbackCorrect: This preserves the actual service task, reporting responsibility and information limits without declaring a violation.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Proof about a condition is not the missing answer to conflicting notices and cannot gate reporting. An apology conversation cannot postpone the supervisor’s immediate Policy 1436 duty. Publishing the disclosure exposes irrelevant health information rather than establishes credibility. Keep both actual responsible processes available.

items.text: Clarify the two conflicting notice instructions through the responsible role.
Ask only the information needed for the present question.
A supervisor immediately reports the protected-class allegation to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer.
Retain assigned agency investigation procedures and non-retaliation.
Demand a treatment update before discussing the notice.
Wait for an apology to decide whether a manager report is needed.

lessons.next: Build an honest follow-through account without measuring personal health or gratitude.

scenario.context: Practice DHS visit: Jules asks about contradictory notices and alleges that a staff member mocked the disclosed condition. The supervisor suggests waiting for an informal apology.
options: Delay reporting while the team decides whose intent was good.
Immediately report the allegation to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer, follow agency procedures and coordinate appropriate notice clarification without unnecessary health disclosure.
Stop every service response until Jules supplies a complete treatment history.
responses: Intent discussion cannot substitute for immediate reporting or actual procedures.
This retains the concern process and current service task without claiming an investigative finding.
A treatment history is not the missing notice information or a prerequisite to manager reporting.

lessons.transfer: Using the practice notice case, separate the service question, allegation, responsible roles and information that is unnecessary to the account.

move.control: Keep an actual concern and current appropriate service response distinct and responsive.
move.failure: A health stereotype or informal-resolution gate displaces the service question and actual reporting duty.
move.next: Practice the immediate manager response and relevant service clarification in the practice case; assigned procedures remain.

lessons.title: Follow through without scoring personal health
lessons.summary: Recognize a specific improvement, retain unfinished responsibilities and keep private support use out of performance measures.
lessons.objective: Describe limited evidence of changed communication without asserting a health outcome or universal absence of stigma.
objectives: Describe limited evidence of changed communication without asserting a health outcome or universal absence of stigma.
Distinguish voluntary support use from a work-performance measure or formal accommodation responsibility.
Choose a follow-through account that preserves unresolved matters, privacy and intrinsic personal learning.
takeaways: A revised note or favorable comment does not prove improved health or eliminate every barrier.
Voluntary support use is not the measure of job performance.
Keep actual open responsibilities and private learning distinct from a public success story.
lessons.statement: An honest account can recognize useful change without claiming what has not been examined.

image.caption: People take part in a discussion with notes and a whiteboard. Their visible participation is not a measurement of well-being or the effects of a program.

intro.heading: Recognize the change and the limits of the evidence
intro.body:
In the practice team’s follow-through, the planning note now describes contradictory deadlines and citation review without diagnostic shorthand. Two colleagues say the revised note is clearer. Rowan’s accommodation request has been carried through the actual decision process but is not yet settled in this example. Jules’s notice question and allegation remain with their appropriate roles. These are different states of the work, not one completed mental-health outcome.

A colleague asks whether the course has reduced anxiety, removed stigma and made every team member comfortable seeking help. The two comments cannot answer those questions. They concern one revised note. No health outcome, complete participation account or broader effect has been established. A quiet team member’s absence of comment is missing feedback, not evidence of well-being, satisfaction or opposition. Even a voluntary thank-you would be a person’s account, not a clinical measurement.

The team can state the specific wording change, the two relevant comments and the responsibilities still open. It should not publish individual health information or a list of who used counseling to make the story look persuasive. MMB’s supervisor referral guidance says Employee Assistance Program use is voluntary and must not be referenced in a performance evaluation. A support offer stays distinct from the employee’s work evidence and actual accommodation process.

MMB’s confidentiality statement explains that LifeMatters contact is not shared outside the service without the client’s written permission, with the stated safety-related legal exception. Employees may use the service anonymously. This is the provider’s actual information practice, not a guarantee that an ordinary colleague’s conversation has the same confidentiality rules. Use current official resources for access details rather than inventing a provider, benefit limit or local contact.

Mira may also understand more deeply why Kai values room to speak. That personal learning matters even if no report captures it and no immediate work result changes. It need not become a health disclosure, an assessed orientation or a performance score. Continuing curiosity can coexist with specific service and employment follow-through.

A useful practice return asks what changed, what supports that account, what remains uncertain and which actual role has the next responsibility. This keeps the contribution visible without a universal success claim. You can practice privately at your own pace and leave personal understanding unrecorded; actual reporting, service and accommodation duties do not depend on course completion.

inThisLesson: Voluntary support and actual confidentiality limits.
Continuing work and learning through private reflection.
lessons.keyStatement: Keep the supported change, unknown effect and actual open responsibility separate.

flashcards.back: A statement about the specific material or encounter examined, no broader than its evidence.
A response not received; it does not establish comfort, distress or satisfaction.
A personal choice about a resource, not a job-performance measure.
An actual unresolved task or process carried by its appropriate role, not erased by a favorable comment.

accordion.heading: Keep the account useful for the next person

items.title: Two comments have a real but limited meaning
items.body: The comments support that the two readers found the revised note clearer. They do not establish a health improvement or the experience of everyone else. Recognize their specific contribution while leaving wider questions open instead of presenting the note as a clinical intervention.

items.title: A resource offer is not a completion metric
items.body: Counting identifiable counseling users or attaching their choices to evaluations can confuse support with performance and expose private information. Follow the actual EAP and employment guidance. A suitable learning account can describe the resource offered without tracking an individual’s use or assuming that use proves an outcome.

items.title: Open work should still be carried
items.body: Rowan’s request and Jules’s concern have actual responsible processes. A clearer note does not settle them. Keep appropriate status and next responsibility distinct without reproducing private case details in a public course story. Useful learning and formal follow-through can continue together.

tabs.label: A complete success claim
tabs.body: Saying the team is now stigma-free turns one wording improvement and two comments into a finding about every encounter. The account becomes less useful because unresolved service and employment tasks disappear. Name the located change and relevant responses, with broader effects still unexamined.

tabs.label: A private-health score
tabs.body: Recording who sought counseling, how grateful they appeared or an inferred diagnosis shifts the measure from the actual work to a person’s private life. Support should remain voluntary and actual information requirements apply. Relevant work evidence can be considered without turning counseling use into the employee’s performance.

tabs.label: A truthful continuation
tabs.body: The note is clearer to two readers, actual request and concern processes remain open, and some effects are unknown. This account helps the next responsible person continue the work. Mira’s wider understanding can remain private and valuable without being converted into a score or mandatory story.

check.question: Which account best fits the practice follow-through?
check.correct: Describe the specific note change and two comments, keep other effects unknown and retain actual open service and employment responsibilities without tracking personal support use.
wrong: Declare improved mental health because no one complained about the revised note.
Use counseling attendance and gratitude as the work-performance measure.
Erase the useful wording change because other matters remain open.
check.feedbackCorrect: The account recognizes supported progress and retains uncertainty, privacy and actual responsibilities.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Silence does not establish improved health or universal satisfaction. Counseling and gratitude are not the actual job-performance measure and can expose private choices. Open matters do not erase a supported wording improvement. Keep each finding and responsibility at its actual scope.

items.text: Two colleagues described the revised planning note as clearer.
No broader health outcome was examined.
Rowan’s request continues with its appropriate decision process.
Jules’s concern continues under the assigned agency procedures.
No response proves everyone is comfortable seeking care.
Counseling attendance determines commitment and job performance.

lessons.next: Use the job aid to connect clear language, real choice and appropriate follow-through.

scenario.context: Practice follow-through: two readers like the revised note. A colleague proposes collecting staff counseling histories to prove that the program improved mental health.
options: Collect the histories because a stronger story outweighs individual information choices.
Drop every account of improvement because formal matters remain open.
Report the specific note change and limited feedback, leave health effects unmeasured and keep private support use separate from actual responsibilities.
responses: Private health accounts cannot be demanded to strengthen an unsupported outcome story.
Open formal work does not erase a supported communication change.
This retains useful progress, actual processes and information limits without inventing an outcome.

lessons.transfer: Write a short practice account of a specific change, the evidence available, an unexamined effect and the next actual responsibility. Your personal reflection can remain separate and private.

move.control: Recognize supported change without measuring a person’s private health or gratitude.
move.failure: A favorable response or silence becomes a universal health outcome and open work disappears.
move.next: Continue with the actual responsible roles and use private or practice reflection for further learning.

jobAid.subtitle: Respectful language, a fitting choice, fair expectations and honest follow-through.
remember: A stated or presumed condition does not supply every fact about the person or present task.
Use a precise description rather than a diagnosis as an insult or shorthand.
An ordinary offer is not clinical care, compulsory disclosure or a guarantee of secrecy.
Voluntary support use is not a measure of work performance.
Private understanding matters without a personal score, live assignment or health story.

sections.heading: Understand the circumstance
items: Separate what was said or observed from the diagnosis, cause, ability or risk you might infer.
Keep the actual work or service question visible.
Compare supplied individual meanings of support without assigning them to a whole group.

sections.heading: Offer support respectfully
items: Ask what would be useful and allow an appropriate choice to accept, discuss or decline.
Use accurate, respectful words and relevant individual preferences; do not make a single identity style compulsory.

Keep clinical assessment and treatment with qualified care. NIMH identifies 988 for emotional or mental-health crisis support and 911 for life-threatening situations; retain actual emergency procedures.

sections.heading: Retain actual employment and concern roles
items: A request for a needed work change because of a medical condition can use ordinary initial words. Promptly forward to the appropriate decision-maker and simultaneously notify the requestor through actual agency authority.
Supervisors and managers do not request accommodation medical information or documentation. Appropriate requests belong to the ADA Coordinator, and medical records are not accepted for this process.

Managers and supervisors immediately report protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures. Staff are strongly encouraged to use the policy’s reporting channels.
Keep a voluntary EAP offer separate from discipline, performance evaluation and the actual accommodation process.

sections.heading: Continue honestly
items: Describe the specific change and available evidence without claiming unexamined health outcomes or universal absence of stigma.
Missing comments and gratitude cannot establish every person’s experience.
Carry remaining tasks through their actual roles and protect personal information under actual requirements.
Let private personal understanding remain unrecorded; no actual case or disclosure is required for this learning.

sources.title: National Institute of Mental Health: caring for your mental health
sources.note: Basic mental-health context, individual self-care and qualified care resources. This course does not diagnose, prescribe treatment or use symptom duration as a gate to help.

sources.title: CDC/NIOSH: stigma-free mental-health communication
sources.note: Healthcare-worker communication guidance supports respectful language and avoiding pressure to share personal stories. Its healthcare-specific research figures are not claims about DHS staff.

sources.title: CDC: preferred terms in health communication
sources.note: The mental-health section guides precise, respectful wording and distinguishes diagnosed conditions from distress. Individual preferred language still matters; this is not a diagnostic or mandatory terminology rule.

sources.title: EEOC: mental health conditions at work
sources.note: Technical assistance on employment, stereotypes, privacy and possible accommodation; actual determinations remain case-specific. State Policy 1433 retains its own designated documentation and decision roles.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1433: reasonable accommodation
sources.note: Actual initial request, prompt forwarding and notice, agency authority, ADA Coordinator consultation and confidential documentation responsibilities.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1436: harassment and discrimination prohibited
sources.note: Actual protected-class concerns and manager/supervisor immediate reporting to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer, with agency procedures and non-retaliation.

sources.title: Council of Europe: developing intercultural competence
sources.note: Educational context for varied, learned individual meanings, perspective-taking and personal understanding. This is not Minnesota policy or an individual intercultural assessment.

sources.title: MMB: guidance when an employee may need help
sources.note: Actual supervisor guidance distinguishes an offer of voluntary support from discipline and performance evaluation; clinical diagnosis is not the supervisor’s role.

sources.title: MMB: employee well-being confidentiality
sources.note: Actual LifeMatters information limits, written-permission requirement and stated legal safety exception. An ordinary colleague conversation does not inherit these provider-specific rules.
